Title: [MODE] UV EDITOR: Bake Textures
Content: Objective Bake selected texture. Location UV Editor Mode Tool Bar Bake Textures Tool Operation Follow the path indicated in the Location above. The Bake Textures setting window will be displayed. Set values according to the table below. Bake Textures Detail Setting Table Saving Path Click folder button to set the file path and save path. Select PNG either JPEG file format. With PNG save option, the background will be transparent. With JPEG save option, the background will be black. Size (pixels) Set the size of the image to be saved. Images are stored in squares of the same horizontal and vertical size. Fill Texture Seams (ver. 2024.1) Set how many pixels to pad the UV shells by. Min: 1 ~ Max: 256 Pixels Infinite Seams (ver. 2024.1) UV Seam Padding is extended to infinity. UV area 0-1 (Default) Save default 0 to 1 tile. A tile is a rectangular area for one section of one unit. Selected tile Save a specific tile. Input U, V location to be saved. All tile Save all tiles that contain UV. Fill Texture Seams The outline is filled with texture as you enter the pixels. Texture type Select texture types to be saved. 3. After setting the details, click the "Save" button at the bottom. The image is baked and saved to the path you set. Note: When baking, the seamline normal map will be baked together. (ver.10) The UV map of the OBJ topstitch used in a garment is also provided. (ver.11) UV padding pixel value can be adjusted using Fill Texture Seams value. The extended seam can also be set to infinite and will not invades other UV shells. (ver. 2024.1) View UV Maps (ver. 10) Upper left of the UV Editor window Click the View UV Map icon Map icons that can be changed appear horizontally. Click the desired map icon. The UV of the 2D window changes to the type of map users click. NOTE View and Bake Displacement Map is now available (ver. 11)

Title: Video Capture (ver. 2024.0)
Content: Video Capture (ver. 2024.0) Capture a video of recorded animation to view in real time. Steps 1. Open the Animation Editor. 2. Record the animation. 3. Select Video Capture from any of the locations below Main Menu Animation Video Capture Animation Editor Toolbar Video Capture Timeline Menu (Right Click) Video Capture 4. Set the video recording properties. Display Size preset Set the size of the video that will be recorded. The format is shown below. 1920 X 1080 (16:9) 1280 X 720 (16:9) 800 X 450 (16:9) 1024 X 768(4:3) 640 X 480(4:3) Fit to Window : Size of 3D Window Custom Full Screen : Monitor Size Width Set the width of the video to be recorded Height Set the height of the video to be recorded File Format Set the format of the file to save. Window : MP4 / AVI MacOS : MP4 / MOV Save as File Name Name the video. Saving path Specify the location where you want to save the video. Autoseq Numbering The video name is automatically saved with a new number. 5. Click the Capture button. The Capture is executed. When executing capture, the capture button will change to a stop button, and the capture process can be terminated with the stop button. End Result 1. Check the captured video The frame range captured will match the playback start and end in the Animation Editor Settings. If the capture in terminated mid execution, start frame to time terminated will be captured. When the capture ends, the video will be automatically launched to the set media player in your computer. Note: You cannot run video capture without animation. You can only capture the movement of the camera in the 3D Window

Title: Animation Keyframe and Layer Editing (ver. 12)
Content: Objective The inclusion of keyframes for simulation caches and keyframe editing tools allow users to fix isolated simulation issues, blend simulations together, adjust timing, and create looping cloth simulation caches. Edit Animation Keyframes Location Animation Editor Animation Timeline Operation Beginning with an avatar with animation, navigate to the Animation Editor. Press the 'Record' button, then stop recording when desired by pressing the 'Record' button again. Select the Animation Layer created for the garment in the Animation Timeline Where vertical lines exist marking Keyframes, select a Keyframe and delete it by pressing the 'Delete' Key. Observe that there is no longer a Keyframe in the previously selected position, and the simulation interpolates vertex positions for the garment linearly across the gap. Where there is now an empty space between Keyframes, move the playtime slider to this position. Select a pattern or garment in the 3D Window. Using the Gizmo, rotate or translate the pattern/garment into a new position. The user can also activate simulation in the 3D Window before creating a new Keyframe. While the playtime slider is still at the position without a keyframe, add a new Keyframe with the 'S' Hotkey. Slide the playtime slider across the area of the timeline where a new frame was keyed, and observe the saved change in the updated frame keyed by the user. To form a smoother transition between the preexisting cache animation and the user-created Keyframe, delete simulation cache Keyframes to the left and right of the user-created Keyframe. Note: Fit the Frame Range - Click the 'Fit Horizontal' button located next to the 'Animation Max Frame' input field at the bottom right of the Animation Editor. This will display every animation layer from its start to end. - Double-click the Animation timeslider to switch to the full layer view. (ver.2024.0) Copy &amp Paste Keyframes Location Animation Editor Animation Timeline Operation Beginning with an avatar with animation, navigate to the Animation Editor. Press the 'Record' button, then stop recording when desired by pressing the 'Record' button again. 'LMB Click' to select a single Keyframe, or 'Shift + LMB Click and Drag' to select multiple Keyframes. If a range of Keyframes has been selected, the user can 'LMB Click and Drag' the white handles on either side of the selection to make fine adjustments. Once the desired selection has been achieved, 'RMB Click' over the highlighted selection to open a pop-up menu then select 'Copy Keyframe' to store the selected frame(s). Move the playtime slider to a different position on the timeline in the same Animation Layer and 'RMB Click' then select 'Paste Keyframe' to past the Keyframe(s) beginning from the current position. Animation Editor Keyframe Options: Create Keyframe 'S' Delete Keyframe 'Del' Copy Keyframe 'Ctrl+C' Paste Keyframe 'Ctrl+V' Cut &amp Merge Animation Layer Location Animation Editor Animation Timeline Operation Cut Animation Layer Beginning with an avatar with animation, navigate to the Animation Editor. Press the 'Record' button, then stop recording when desired by pressing the 'Record' button again. Select the resulting Animation Layer by clicking on its title at the left of the Animation Editor interface. Move the playtime slider to a point in the middle of the resulting Animation Layer. Press the 'Cut' button in the Animation Editor Toolbar (scissor icon). Observe that the Animation Layer has split at the current timeline position, and the portion removed has been separated into a new Animation Layer. Merge Animation Layers Select two Animation layers by clicking on their titles at the left of the Animation Editor interface while holding the 'Shift' Key. Press the 'Merge' button in the Animation Editor Toolbar (two overlapping squares) to Merge the Animation Layers together. Animation Layers can be moved horizontally (see below) before being merged together to adjust timing. When merging layers, the layers will be merged into the top selected layers. Animation Layer Controls Location Animation Editor Animation Layer Operation Move Animation Layer Horizontally Double LMB click on the interpolation space of an Animation Layer (solid pink by default) to activate track movement. When the interpolation space of an Animation Layer is highlighted (red by default), the layer can be moved left and right by clicking and dragging with the mouse cursor. To move the Animation Layer to a specific number of frames, when highlighted, RMB clicks on the Animation layer and select 'Move Layer Horizontally', then enter the desired number of frame units to move the Animation Layer. When highlighted, an Animation Layer can also be moved one frame unit at a time by using the Left or Right Arrow Keys. Delete Animation Layer To the left of the Animation Timeline, click on the name of the Animation Layer you would like to delete - highlighting it in grey - and click the "Delete" Key to delete the entire Animation Layer Reorder Animation Layer To the left of the Animation Timeline, click on the name of the Animation Layer you would like to move and drag it above or below the Animation Layer. Animation data for an Animation Layer on top will completely block any animation data on an Animation Layer beneath. Layer Locking &amp Keyframe Visibility Lock an Animation Layer by clicking ON the leftmost yellow circle next to the desired Animation Layer's name. Hide an Animation Layer's cached animation by clicking OFF the center yellow circle next to the desired Animation Layer's name. Hide an Animation Layer's keyframe markers by clicking OFF the rightmost yellow circle next to the desired Animation Layer's name. Animation Layer Selection To select an Animation Layer, click on its title to the left of the animation timeline (it will turn a lighter shade of grey when selected). To add another Animation Layer to the selection, hold down the 'Shift' Key and click on the title of an additional layer. To remove an Animation Layer from the selection, hold down the 'Ctrl' Key and click on the title of any Animation Layer you would like to deselect. Rename Animation layer To rename an animation layer, double-click on its name or right-click on the name of the animation layer and select 'Rename'. Hold down the Shift key to select multiple animation layers, and then follow the above steps to rename them all at once. Animation Editor UI Updates Location Animation Editor Animation Editor Toolbar Operation Animation Editor Icon Additions &amp Updates: Loop Circular Arrow Sets animation timeline playback to loop. Playback Speed 1X Ranges from 1/4X to 8X speed. Merge Selected Animation Layers Two Overlapping Squares Merge selected Animation Layers into a single layer. Cut Selected Animation Layer Scissors Split Animation Layer at current timeline position. Delete Trash Can Deletes Animation Layer or Keyframe depending on selection. Create Keyframe I Creates new Keyframe at current timeline position.

Title: [Mode] Animation
Content: Objective Record garment animation. Location Main Menu Change the mode at the top-right corner ANIMATION Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Change the mode at the top-right corner ANIMATION Animation window appears. Note: 'Complete' increases number of simulation checks to process the avatar and garment more precisely. It is recommended to set the Simulation Quality to 'Complete' to stabilize the animation as motion data increases garment collision when recording it. Title: ANIMATION MODE: Garment Animation Making
Content: Objective Tips for creating stable and realistic garment animation for multi-layered garments. Operation Optimize 3D Garment for Animation The heavier the garment, the slower and harder it records. Follow the steps below to make it lighter. For a multi-layered garment, increase particle distance to 20mm for inner layers that are not as visible as outer layers. Delete invisible and any other unnecessary layers. Outer layers: Set the particle distance to 10mm for parts that does not require higher level of expression of wrinkles. Set the particle distance to 5mm for parts that require higher level of expression of wrinkles. If there is large quantity of layers set to 5mm, set all of them to 7mm. Fix Garment If garment is not fixed to avatar while recording the animation, the garment moves drastically around the avatar due to collision. Certain parts of the garment need to be fixed to the avatar or itself to create more realistic recording. Use functions such as 'Avatar Tape' or 'Tack on Avatar' to attach shoulder and sides of the garment. Use 'Tack' function for overlapped layers or any parts that may dangle. Increase Transition Animation Time Increase the transition animation time for heavier garments. In the animation dialogue, enter 5FPS to stabilize the simulation. This makes the avatar movement slower which helps to minimize the collision between the garments. Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for the First Recording Setting Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' minimizes the collision between the avatar and garments. To save time, the simulation quality can be set to 'Normal' for the middle part of the recording as the avatar and garments tend to collide more in the beginning and end. Make sure the simulation to set the quality back on 'Complete' for the end of the Transition Animation. Reevaluate Draping of the Garment after the Recording As the avatar moves, some parts of the garment may collide. When the simulation is off, the 3D garment may appear fine, however there is possibility of unnoticeable collision which may destabilize rest of the recording. Return to Simulation Mode. Note: From ver2.5.0, it is possible to simulate by pressing the Simulation button without recording it. Active simulation and make sure the entire garment simulation is stable. If any parts of the garment is unstable, readjust the layers by using the Select/Move tool. Once the simulation has been stabilized, go back to the Animation Mode. Set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' when Recording the Actual Garment Animation Make sure to set Simulation Quality status on 'Complete' for final recordings of Garment Animation as the 'Complete' and the 'Normal' give clearly different results in expressing reality.

Title: ANIMATION MODE: Record Animation
Content: Objective Record garment animation. Note: Follow the link Process of Making Garment Animation for your reference on creating garment animation in details. Location Animation Mode Animation Editor Record Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Animation Mode Animation Editor Record Simulation turns on automatically and it is now being recorded in frames. If a Transition Animation is created, the recording automatically stops at the end of the Transition Animation frame and starts again (ver2.5.0). Note: Transition Animation is auto-generated animation tool which automatically generates for stabilizing transition when the original Avatar pose is different to the first pose in the motion file. Once the garment and avatar arrive in a new position, it is no longer in need therefore the recording automatically stops for you to delete this unnecessary part. The Transition Animation for default avatars of version10 is not compatible with the previous versions. 2. Once the Avatar's motion ends, the recording automatically stops. To stop the recording while it is in process, click the Pause button. Copy Frame The feature is to create assets for Dynamic Wrinkle. (ver. 5.1.445) - After recording an animation of a garment and copy /paste on designated frame.

Title: ANIMATION MODE: Wind Animation
Content: Save Wind animation property by frame (Ver. MD 7) Objective Create or delete wind animation key Location Animation Mode Animation Editor Operation Creating Wind Animation Key Create a pattern to apply Wind animation. Navigate to the menu indicated in Location. Main menu&gtDisplay&gtEnvironment&gt Check 'Show Wind Controller' Can adjust wind property when Wind Controller is displayed. Select the Wind controller and move Playhead to the frame where Wind animation key will be applied on Timeline Wind controller will move along intermediate value if move Playhead after Wind animation key is set, Need to move Playhead first before set wind property, in order to locate wind controller to desired position. Wind property will displayed when select Wind controller on 3D window. Use Gizmo to adjust Wind controller's position and direction. Check properties want to apply and input value. Rotation and position of the wind are available to adjust by Gizmo on 3D window. Right click on Playhead on time line. Select 'Add key' on popup menu to save wind property. Add key menu will not show up if wind controller is not selected. When Wind Animation key is set, Wind property values will be applied gradually to the next key. For example, if Wind strength of first frame is 500 and last frame is 1000, Wind strength will gradually increase 500 ~ 1000 from first frame to last frame. When Wind Animation key is set and there is no existing next Wind animation key, Wind property of the key will be applied from the key to the end of the frame. Wind Property will be applied when recording animation. Checking Wind Animation Key Check position and rotation of wind controller of each frame by moving Playhead on time line, after adding Wind Animation key on 3D window. Deleting key Select Wind controller. Wind Animation keys will be displayed on Animation timeline. Select a key and right click. Select 'Delete Key' on pop up menu to delete selected Wind Animation key. Available to delete multiple keys by Area select. Move Playhead to the start point of desired area and click the end of the area while pressing 'Shift' key. Delete all key of selected area by right click on selected area&gt select Delete Key on popup menu.

Title: Lock Remesh Patterns
Content: Objective Lock patterns from selection based on whether or not they are dynamic Marvelous Designer patterns with adjustable particle distance and curve points, or remeshed patterns created with the Topology Tools &amp Remesh All. Location 2D Pattern Window Lock Pattern Drop-down Menu Lock All Remesh Patterns Operation Load a garment. Create topology with the 'Create Topology' Tool in the 2D Pattern Window. When complete, with blue retopology still visible, Right Mouse Button Click in the 2D Pattern Window then select 'Remesh All (duplicate)'. Retopology meshes are placed directly on top of the original patterns. Click on 'Lock All Remesh Patterns' in the Lock Pattern drop-down menu within the 2D Window to lock all remeshed patterns from selection. Click and move original patterns as desired with the 'Transform Pattern' Tool. Click on 'Unlock All Remesh Patterns' to release the selection mask. Click on 'Lock All Pattern Outlines' and 'Lock All Internal Lines' to lock original patterns from selection. Click and move remeshed patterns as desired with the 'Transform Pattern' Tool.

Title: Marvelous Designer 12 Retopology Improvements
Content: Objective Improve the flexibility and ease of use of the Topology Tools within Marvelous Designer. Create Topology: Location 3D/2D Window Tool Bar Topology Tools New Operation (from Ver.12) Cut Topology Faces Existing blue topology faces can be split by drawing new Topology Points/Edges across them. If cut faces result in Ngons, any blue topology faces with more than 4 sides will be highlighted in orange. User-Drawn Topology snaps to Internal Lines When the user creates topology, new points can be snapped to Internal Lines/Shapes as well as external pattern boundaries. Edit Topology: Location 3D/2D Windows Tool Bar Edit Topology Tool New Operation (from Ver.12) Display Ghost Topology across Sewing Relationships for Internal Lines When Topology Points meet Internal Lines with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing relationship. Drag Select Topology Points Click outside of an area of blue topology and drag across it to select multiple Topology Points at once. Click and hold the 'Shift' Key, then click and drag over an additional area of blue topology to add Topology Points to an existing selection. Drag Deselect Topology Points Click and hold the 'Control' Key, then click and drag over an existing selection of Topology Points to remove Topology Points from that selection. Patch Topology: Location 2D Window Tool Bar Patch Topology Tool New Operation (from Ver.12) Snap Patch Topology to Internal Shapes/Lines Patch Topology edges will snap to both external and internal pattern lines and curve points. Snap Patch Topology to Convex Curves Patch Topology edges will now snap to both concave and convex curves. If the curvature of an edge is too extreme for a patch to be created, add one or several curve points along the curved edge with the 'Add Point/Split Line' tool to divide the curve into sections with less extreme curvature. Evaluate Patch Validity at Creation After closing a Topology Patch and clicking 'Create', if the drawn patch would create overlapping geometry, an error window pop-up will be raised - return to the Patch Topology tool and update the patch as necessary to avoid overlapping edges/vertices. If the drawn patch would not result in overlapping geometry, the Topology Patch will be created and displayed in blue.

Title: Retopology (ver. 12 & Above)
Content: Objective Allow the user to draw topology lines onto existing patterns creating a new mesh with a lower polygon count and edge-loops optimized for animation. Create Topology Location 3D/2D Window Tool Bart Topology Tools Operation Follow the path indicated in Location above. When a Topology tool selected, patterns will be displayed as transparent. When you place the mouse cursor over a pattern, the pattern is highlighted in its original color. New topology can only be created on one pattern at a time. Click on the highlighted pattern to add a topology point. Topology can be created in both the 2D and 3D Windows, though we recommend using the 2D Window primarily. Creating Face When creating Topology lines, a Topology face is created if a closed shape is drawn. Topology faces are created only on shapes with 3 or 4 points/sides. To stop drawing Topology before closing a shape (leaving an open shape), double-click to finish. Cancel point creation Cancel points one-by-one by pressing Delete/Backspace Key on the keyboard. Cancel all points: Press ESC, Ctl + Z Key on the keyboard. Add Division Loop While hovering over an edge with the Create Topology Tool, press Shift + Ctrl and click to add an edge loop across continuous faces. Additional Operation (Above Ver.12) Cut Topology Faces Existing blue topology faces can be split by drawing new Topology Points/Edges across them. If cut faces result in Ngons, any blue topology faces with more than 4 sides will be highlighted in orange. Edit Topology Location 3D/2D Windows Tool Bar Edit Topology Tool Operation Follow the path indicated in the Location above. Existing topology is highlighted in sky blue after selecting the Edit Topology Tool and Place the mouse cursor over a pattern with existing topology. Select a Topology point, line, or face, and edit it by holding and moving it, or deleting it with the Delete Key. Point/ Line / Face multi-selection While holding the Shift or the Ctrl Key, click on multiple topology points/lines one at a time to add them to a selection. 2D point drag selection While pressing Ctrl key on the keyboard and drag to select multiple topology points. Line loop selection Double click a topology line to loop select. Delete Point/ Line/ Face Press Delete key on the keyboard or right-click and select the delete menu to delete Point/ Line/ Face. Extrude Select lines, press Shift + Ctrl and drag to Extrude. Right-click popup menu Right-click on a point, line, face, pattern or background to access the popup menus. The menu that appears may vary depending on what is applied. Delete Delete selected object. Show Topology Only (3D) Display only the topology, excluding garments or other objects. Show All Unhide everything in the scene in 3D window. Merge Merge two or more points. Merge All Merge all topology points by distance. Set the distance between topology points and click the apply button to merge. Click the close button to close the dialog. Add Division (Current Pattern) Add division on a selected pattern. Adds one division level at a time. Add All Division Add division to entire Topology face. (right-click on the background to pop-up this menu) Remesh (duplicate) Convert (Duplicate) (ver. 2024.0) Duplicate a new mesh based on created topology face. (Applied per pattern) Remesh All (duplicate) Convert All (Duplicate) (ver. 2024.0) Duplicate a new mesh based on created topology face of the entire pattern. Remesh (replace) Convert (Replace) (ver. 2024.0) Delete an existing pattern and create a new mesh based on created topology face. (Applied per pattern) Remesh All (replace) Convert All (Replace) (ver. 2024.0) Delete the entire pattern and create new mesh based on created topology face. Show/ Hide Show/ Hide created Topology from 3D Main menu Display 3D garment Show topology. Topology Ghost Display/Snapping Based on The Sewing Lines (Above Ver.11) When Topology Points meet pattern edges with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing relationship. These ghost Topology Points help you snap any new topology you create across sewing relationships to exactly the same place as the existing topology on patterns across the seam. Additional Operation (Above Ver.12) Topology Ghost Display/Snapping across Sewing Relationships for Internal Lines When Topology Points meet Internal Lines with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing relationship. Drag Select Topology Points Click outside of an area of blue topology and drag across it to select multiple Topology Points at once. Click and hold the 'Shift' Key, then click and drag over an additional area of blue topology to add Topology Points to an existing selection. Drag Deselect Topology Points Click and hold the 'Control' Key, then click and drag over an existing selection of Topology Points to remove Topology Points from that selection. Patch Topology Location 2D Window Tool Bar Patch Topology Tool Operation (Above Ver.11) Navigate to the interface/menu Location above. Select the 'Patch Topology' Tool, and a pop-up box will appear where you can adjust the number of subdivisions for an edge. Subdivisions Adjust the number of edge subdivisions Patch Style (ver. 2024.1) Grid Grid is the legacy algorithm which obtains more linear results. Uniform A new algorithm which obtains results with more natural flow and smaller size differences. Create After the patch shape is closed, click the 'Create' button, and the patch lines will turn into topology faces. Clear Delete all in-progress patch lines. Create patch lines on a 2D pattern. Internal topology will appear divided into the preset number of subdivisions along edges, if a a closed patch section is either triangular or rectangular. You can change the number of subdivisions for the next edge while a Topology Patch is in progress (before the patch shape is closed). You can also change the number of subdivisions after closing a patch section (but before clicking 'Create') by selecting the completed patch edge and changing the number in the 'Subdivisions' field. Additional Operation (Above Ver.12) Snap Patch Topology to Internal Shapes/Lines Patch Topology edges will snap to both external and internal pattern lines and curve points. Snap Patch Topology to Convex Curves Patch Topology edges will now snap to both concave and convex curves. If the curvature of an edge is too extreme for a patch to be created, add one or several curve points along the curved edge with the 'Add Point/Split Line' tool to divide the curve into sections with less extreme curvature. Evaluate Patch Validity at Creation After closing a Topology Patch and clicking 'Create', if the drawn patch would create overlapping geometry, an error window pop-up will be raised - return to the Patch Topology tool and update the patch as necessary to avoid overlapping edges/vertices. If the drawn patch would not result in overlapping geometry, the Topology Patch will be created and displayed in blue. Note: The algorithm for patch topology has been improved, resulting in a more efficient mesh. (ver. 2024.0) In the case of a square with the same number of points on each side, the results for both Grid and Uniform patch styles are the same. (ver. 2024.1)

Title: Remeshing to Retopology (Selected)  (ver. 5.1.4)
Content: Objective Remesh selected pattern and generate retopology lines along the remeshed polygon. Location Right-click pattern pop-up menu (3D window) Remeshing to Retopology Operation Click the menu specified in Location. A polygon count input dialog will pop up. Enter the desired number of polygons and click the Apply button. The mesh of the selected patterns is rearranged into an aligned quad mesh. Retopology lines are generated along the remeshed polygons. To return to the previous status, right-click on the pattern and select 'Undo Remeshing' from the pop-up menu.

Title: Retopology (ver 5.1.0)

(Applied per pattern) Remesh All (duplicate) Duplicate a new mesh based on created topology face of the entire pattern. (Applied per pattern) Remesh All (replace) Delete the entire pattern and create new mesh based on created topology face. Show/Hide Show/Hide created Topology from 3D Main menu Display 3D garment Show topology. Topology Ghost Display/Snapping Based on The Sewing Lines (Above Ver.11) When there are topology points at a pattern edge with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing line. These ghost topology points help you snap any new topology you create across sewing relationships to exactly the same place as your existing topology. Patch Topology (Above Ver.11) Location 2D Window Tool Bar Patch Topology Tool Operation Follow the Location above. Select the Edit Patch Topology Tool, and a pop-up box appears, where you can adjust the number of subdivisions. Subdivisions Adjust the number of subdivisions Create After all of the sections are closed, click the 'Create' button, and the patch lines will turn into topology faces. Clear Delete all in-progress patch lines. Create patch lines on a 2D pattern. - Internal topology dash lines will appear divided into the preset number of subdivisions, if a patch section is either triangular or rectangular. - You can change the number of subdivisions before closing a patch section. - You can also change the number of subdivisions after closing a patch section by selecting the completed patch line.

Title: Binding (ver. 11)
Content: Create Binding Objective Easily create Binding along Pattern Outlines. Location Main Menu Materials Binding Binding 3D Toolbar Binding Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Pattern Outlines and Internal Lines where Binding can be created appear in dashed lines. 2. On a 3D Garment or 2D Pattern, click the start point and double click where you want to finish the Binding. Binding is created on the selected segment. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Select Binding Objective Edit Binding Properties. Location Main Menu Materials Binding Select Binding 3D Toolbar Select Binding Note: 3D toolbar Select bindings with the Select/Move tool. Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. The line segment for which the binding was created is displayed. 2. Select the Binding to be edited. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Configure each property as needed referring to below table. Option Description Name Rename Binding's name. Line Length Check Binding's length. However, it cannot be changed from the Property Editor. Type Under Bindings are placed under the Patterns to express Inside Bindings. Over Bindings are placed over the Patterns. Both Bindings are placed both direction of the Patterns. Dimension Width Adjust selected Binding's width. (1~50mm) Length Adjust selected Binding's length with percentage (50% ~ 200%) or a specific value. Particle Distance Edit selected Binding's Particle Distance (4~20mm) Add'l Thickness - Collision Adjust Binding's Add'l Thickness - Collision. Fabric Assign Fabric to the Binding. Fabric styles in the Fabric Object Browser appear in a list. Grain Direction Bias/ Warp/ Custom Choose among Bias, Warp, or Custom for the Binding's grain direction. Angle Manually insert Angle value to set the Binding's grain direction. Topstitch Add Topstitch to the Binding. The Topstitch option shows the styles which are added in the Topstitch tab of Object Browser. Sewing Line Type Edit Binding's Sewing Line Type. Extend Set whether to extend the binding after creating it on a part of the line segment. Note: Binding Extension is not possible in the following cases. When the angle of both segments are more than 180 degrees based on the binding start/end point. 4. Right-click on the Binding to be edited. Option Description Delete Delete selected Binding. Reset Arrangement Reset Binding's position. Use this option to fix unstable simulations. Deactivate / Activate Deactivate or activate selected Binding. Freeze / Unfreeze Freeze or unfreeze selected Binding. Flip Normal The selected Binding's face flips to the other side.

Title: Create Piping
Content: Objective Create piping along with Garment seamlines. Location Main Menu Materials Piping Piping 3D Toolbar Piping Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Dash-lines appear along the edges of the Garment where piping is applicable. On a 3D Garment or 2D Pattern (ver MD10), click the desired starting point, drag to extend, then double click to complete the Piping. The Piping is now being created as designed. Note: To create Piping on the entire circumference of a single Pattern, click on the first point of the Pattern outline click on the second point click back on the first point.

Title: Edit Piping Length
Content: Objective Edit the length of Piping. Location Main Menu Materials Piping Edit Piping 3D Toolbar Edit Piping Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Piping Edit Piping 3D Toolbar Edit Piping An editable line appears on top of all Piping, and also a hidden Piping appears in semi-transparent temporarily. Click and drag on either end point of the editable line to adjust the length.

Title: Show/Hide Piping
Content: Objective Show or hide all Piping. Location 3D Window Garment Show/Hide Icon (Mouse Over) Show Piping Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window Garment Show/Hide Icon (Mouse Over) Show Piping All created Piping is now being hidden. Follow the indicated guideline again: 3D Window Garment Show/Hide Icon (Mouse Over) Show Piping All hidden Piping is now being displayed again.

Title: Modify Piping Status
Content: Objective Modify Piping status. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move or Edit Piping Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move or Edit Piping Right click on a desired piping to edit. Piping pop-up menu appears. Pop-up Menu Definition Delete Delete the selected Piping. Refresh All Piping Re-drape all Piping. Deactivate/Activate Deactivate/Activate selected Piping. Freeze/Unfreeze Freeze/Unfreeze selected Piping. Quadranglate Change Piping mesh to quads. Triangulate Change Piping mesh to triangles. Hide Hide selected Piping. Show All Piping Show all Piping.

Title: ZIPPER: Assign Different Materials to Slider, Puller, Stopper & Teeth
Content: Objective Allows for different materials to be assigned to different components of the zipper individually, giving the user more control over the look of their garment's fine details. Location 3D Window Zipper Property Editor Material Operation Load garment. Add Zipper with the Zipper Tool in the 3D Window Toolbar. Select the Zipper Slider in the 3D Window. Navigate to the Property Editor. Under the 'Material' section, change the 'Type' to the desired material type. Under Material Basic Parameters Texture, change the texture to the desired color or texture file. Select the Zipper Puller in the 3D Window Navigate to the Property Editor. Under the 'Material' section, change the 'Type' to the desired material type. Under Material Basic Parameters Texture, change the texture to the desired color or texture file. Observe that the material on the Zipper Slider is different from the material on the Zipper Puller.

Title: ZIPPER: Register Custom OBJ as Slider & Puller
Content: Objective Allows the user to create custom components for zippers that function dynamically in the 3D Window exactly as default provided zipper components. Location Main Menu Materials Zipper Register OBJ 3D Toolbar Zipper Tool Property Editor Shape '+' Operation Create mesh for Zipper Puller or Slider and export as an OBJ. If creating a single OBJ file for both Slider &amp Puller, the node for the Slider must be named "Slider," and the node for the Puller must be named "Puller" before export. Navigate to either of the locations listed above under "Location" and click on 'Register OBJ' or the '+' icon in the Property Editor. Select the relevant Type (Slider, Puller, Slider &amp Puller, Stopper). In the File section of the pop-up window, click on the four-square button to navigate to the location of the custom OBJ file and Double-Click to select it. Adjust the position of the Puller or Slider in the preview window. Click 'OK'. Load a garment with a Zipper. Click on the Zipper in the 3D Window. In the Property Editor for the Zipper, observe that the Slider, Puller, or Stopper the user has registered is now available to be assigned to the zipper. You can find the custom Zipper component in the dropdown menu to the right of Slider or Puller under the 'Shape' section.

Title: ZIPPER: Create Zippers
Content: Objective Create and use Zippers quickly and easily. Location Main Menu Materials Zipper Zipper 3D Toolbar Zipper Operation Navigate to the location listed below: 3D Toolbar Zipper Click on the 3D garment or 2D Patterns (ver MD10) where the Zipper should be attached, then move the cursor. Based on the direction the cursor is moved, the segment where the Zipper appears is highlighted in light blue. Double click on the desired endpoint for the Zipper. One side of the Zipper is created. Click on the Pattern outline where the other side of the Zipper is attached, then move the cursor. Based on the direction the cursor is moved, a blue point appears indicating the same length as the first half of the Zipper which was created in step 3. Double click on the blue point. The Zipper is now complete, along with a Puller, Slider, and Stopper (ver MD10). Activate the Simulation. The Zipper simulates in a closed/fully zipped state. To unzip the Zipper, click on the Zipper in the 3D Window WITHOUT the Gizmo active, and drag to move the Zipper (referenced in dark grey) along the length of the Zipper Tape. Note: Cancel Actions during Zipper Creation Cancel All Actions While using the Zipper tool, press 'Esc' or 'Ctlr +Z' on the keyboard, and all actions will be undone. Cancel Last Action While using the Zipper tool, press the 'Delete' or 'Backspace' Key on the keyboard and the last action will be undone.

Title: ZIPPER: Zipper Tape Properties
Content: Objective Modify the Zipper tape properties. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Zipper Tape (Click On Zipper Tape) Property Editor Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Zipper Tape (Click On Zipper Tape) Property Editor The properties of the selected Zipper Tape appear in the Property Editor. Modify the Zipper Tape properties based on the available options below: Properties Description Name Rename the Zipper Tape. Line Length Edit the length of the Zipper teeth. Size (ver.11) Set the size of the Zipper. Teeth Width Enter directly the width of the Zipper to adjust. Total Width Adjust the Tape width of the Zipper. Width Set the width of the Zipper Tape. The texture image changes based on the width entered. Thickness Set the Zipper Tape Thickness. Particle Distance Adjust zipper tape's Particle Distance. Fasten Zipper Zip or unzip the Zipper. Fold Adjust the Strength of the fold for Sewing between the Zipper and Pattern. Material Set the Material Type, Texture, Color and Opacity of the Zipper Teeth and Tape. Physical Property Adjust physical properties to the selected zipper teeth.

Title: ZIPPER: Unzip/ Zip Zippers
Content: Objective Zip or unzip Zippers as needed. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Click &amp drag on the Zipper Slider. The selected Slider is highlighted in yellow. Continue to drag the Slider. The Slider follows and moves along with the cursor. A preview of the new Slider position appears. Release the mouse to the desired position. The Zipper Slider is moved to the new location. Activate the Simulate tool. The Zipper simulates and zips/unzips based on the new location.

Title: ZIPPER: Zipper Slider and Stopper Properties
Content: Objective Modify the Zipper Slider and Stopper (ver MD10) properties. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Operation Select the tool indicated in Location. Select a Zipper or Stopper created on a 3D Garment and modify its properties: Option Description Name Name the zipper. Shape Slider Select a shape for the slider. Puller Select a shape for the puller. Stopper Select the Stopper type (Open / Closed End) and then select shapes for Top and Bottom. (ver MD10) Note: A selection of Bottom shapes is configured based on the shape of the Stopper. Specification Gauge Select the size of the Slider by Gauge or percentage. Weight (g) Assign the weight of the slider. (ver 4.2) Fasten Zipper Reverse Zip Direction Select the zip direction. The slider is relocated based on the option. Move to Opposite Side Select a side of the zipper tape where the slider will locate when the zipper is open. Material Configure the Slider's Type, Texture, Color, and Opacity. Note: Uncheck Use Same Material as Slider after selecting the Puller or Stopper tab to assign material separately. (ver MD10) Note: Adjust the weight of the Slider Polygon Optimization (ver. MD2024.0) Count Set the number of polygons. Plane This is applied in the form of a texture when the Plane is activated. Count cannot be set on Plane activation.

Title: ZIPPER: Zipper/Slider Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
Content: Objective Modify the Zipper or Slider via the right-click pop-up menu. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Right-Click on a Zipper or Slider Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Right-Click on a Zipper or Slider The respective pop-up menu appears for the Zipper or Slider. Adjust the settings below as needed: Zipper Tape Slider Delete Delete the selected Zipper and Zipper Slider. Deactivate Deactivate or activate the selected Zipper and Slider. Freeze Freeze or unfreeze the selected Zipper and Slider. Reverse (Right-Clicked Teeth) Reverse the sewing direction of the Zipper Tape based on the side of the Zipper Tape that was right clicked. n/a Flip Normal (Right-Clicked Teeth) Flip the surface of the side of the Zipper Tape that was right clicked. n/a Reset Slider Arrangement n/a Reset the slider's position and angle to default (ver4.1.0). Show/Hide Slider n/a Show or hide the Slider (ver4.0.0).
